title: Which record owns the scan of STEGO's own Go modules for known vulnerabilities?
description: The workflows check STEGO's own dependencies: go mod verify and govulncheck in checks.yml and runtime-library.yml, and vulnerability-scan.yml (ST-ASR-TOOL06), which scans every Go module on main each week. No design record asks for this, so no test of it can be a proof: the test of the module list in scripts/test_release_publishing.py names no record. Options: (a) a new rule of ST-STD-TRUST: every Go module of STEGO MUST be verified against its go.sum and scanned for known vulnerabilities by each check of the module and on main each week, and a reachable known vulnerability MUST fail the check; its test is the module list test; (b) a UC requirement of an Assuring use case; (c) keep it as tooling with no proof. Recommendation: (a): it is an engineering rule for STEGO's own code, as the rules of ST-STD-TRUST are, and it holds the scan to every module, also one added later.

title: Where does stego build download take the runtime pin of a service, while the runtime library is not released on the public module proxy?
description: Since the archetype move (ST-SUP-RC20-OC39) every generated service imports the runtime library, and the examples do too. stego deps and local builds resolve the pin from the common registry's runtime folder, verified by the pinned hash (ST-SUP-INV10). stego build download runs in a fixed environment with the public module proxy only, and a module that the proxy cannot supply stops it (ST-BLD-UC02-R03). The runtime is not released: no tag registry/runtime/<version> is pushed and stego.dev serves no go-import page for it, so the application build job of CI stops at github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime v0.30.0. Options: (a) the Product owner releases the runtime at each pin: serve the go-import page, push the tag registry/runtime/<version> at the commit whose folder hashes to the pin, and the public proxy then supplies it; (b) stego build download takes the pin from the common registry's runtime folder as stego deps does, as a local file proxy before the public proxy, only when the folder hashes to the pinned sum, and the build record names that source; (c) the application build job builds a service that does not import the runtime until (a). Recommendation: (b) now, because the zip is verified by the pinned hash and so is the same bytes as a release, with (a) at the first release; the build record names the source, so a reviewer sees which builds did not use the public proxy.

title: Can stego build download take the runtime pin from the runtime folder of a STEGO checkout that a flag names, for a source with no runtime folder?
description: Developer walkthrough of 2026-11-13, step 25 (F7): a user project holds no registry/runtime folder, and origin has no registry/runtime/<version> tag, so stego build download cannot get the runtime pin and a clean machine cannot build a generated service. The Product owner chose both remedies: (a) the owner pushes the tags of agents/followup/tag-plan.md, and (b) stego build download takes a flag that names the runtime folder of a STEGO checkout. ST-BLD-UC02-R05 and ST-BLD-CLI02 name only the runtime folder of the source revision. The follow-up worker built (b) as --runtime-folder <folder>: the folder passes every check of R05 (go.sum, the pin that the binary carries, sum.golang.org, no link or special file), and the cache and build records name it as checkout:registry/runtime; it is refused for a source that holds its own runtime folder, for a go.mod with no runtime pin, and for a folder with no go.mod. Proposed restatement of R05, for the owner: When go.mod requires the runtime library and the source revision holds the common registry's runtime folder registry/runtime, or the author names the runtime folder of a STEGO checkout for a source that holds none, the download MUST take that version from that folder only after ... (the rest as today), and the records MUST name which folder supplied it. Proposed addition to ST-BLD-CLI02: [--runtime-folder <stego checkout>/registry/runtime]. Tests ST-BLD-UC02-R05-T10 to T12 prove (b) under R05 until the owner restates it. Decision (orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13): the proposed restatement is accepted. ST-BLD-UC02-R05 and ST-BLD-CLI02 are restated to name --runtime-folder.

title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: How must a change that adds a key to SIGNERS and signs a fill with it be stopped from qualifying its own fill?
description: The security baseline of 2026-11-11 (finding 4) found that qualification reads SIGNERS from the tree it qualifies, so one change can add a key to a SIGNERS file and sign a fill with that key, and the fill is qualified in that change's own checks. ST-EXT-TM04 says that adding a signer is a reviewed change to SIGNERS, but no record makes that review separate from the sign-off it enables. Neither fix is allowed by the records as they are: ST-EXT-SP01 and ST-EXT-UC02-R02 say the project's SIGNERS file, which is the file in the tree, and the compiler runs in a project folder that need not have git or a base ref; and no UC requirement of ST-ASR-UC02 lets the change gate refuse a change for what it does to SIGNERS. Options: (a) qualification reads SIGNERS from a base ref that the caller gives, such as stego plan --signers-ref, and the tree's file only when no ref is given; this changes ST-EXT-SP01 and ST-EXT-UC02-R02 and adds a git dependency to every user project's compile; (b) a new UC requirement of ST-ASR-UC02: the change gate refuses a change that alters a SIGNERS file and adds or changes a fill sign-off in the same tree, naming both files; such a change is split in two, or merges by the owner's review and bypass, as a change to the CI definitions does (ST-ASR-UC02-R06); (c) no code change: CODEOWNERS requires the owner's review of every SIGNERS file, which holds only when the branch rule of the base branch requires code owner review (finding 1, the owner's). Recommendation: (b), with (c) as well: it keeps qualification the same for every user project, it makes the new signer a change of its own that the owner reviews, and the gate already reads both trees. The CODEOWNERS line for **/SIGNERS is in the workflows pull request of this hardening.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: How does the baseline of a retype give back the column of the release before it?
description: The baseline migration 001_initial is the declaration with every schema step undone, and its body digest must be the one in the ledger of the release that runs. A retype keeps only From, the type before the change, so a retyped field that had constraints (max_length, min, max, values, a default or unique) cannot give back its old column, its checks and its indexes, and the baseline digest differs. Options: (a) a retype also takes the Definition of the old field, as a drop does (ST-DECL-EN21, ST-DECL-INV57), and the baseline reads the old column from it; (b) a retype takes From only and the old field must have had no constraint; (c) the baseline is read from the base record, not derived. Recommendation: (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13; it goes into the records and the code with the retype kind (ST-GEN-UC12, part 2b).

title: What does the release with a rename, retype or require at expand read for a row that the backfill has not reached?
description: ST-SUP-RC01-OC12 has the manifest of the release with an open rename, retype or require leave out the old column, so that release reads only the new column, which is NULL in each row that the backfill (ST-GEN-UC13) has not moved yet; for a required field that read fails or loses the value. Options: (a) the api replicas of that release stay not ready until the backfill of each open rename, retype and require is complete, while the release before serves, and the rollout has maxUnavailable 0; (b) the release reads coalesce(new, old) while the change is at expand, and needs the old column, so it cannot restart after the next release's contract (against ST-GEN-INV34); (c) the expand migration fills the new column, which holds one long transaction (rejected in ST-GEN-UC13). Recommendation: (a). Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: readiness reads the backfill status from the database (stego_schema.backfills), never from a flag that the replica sets itself; the rename, retype and require kinds wait for UC13 or for a real backfill status. It goes into the records with the rename kind.

title: How does a release prove that a schema step trigger is its own, so the release before it accepts only a signed step?
description: ST-GEN-Q08 (e) adds a release-signed step record to the strict (c) rules: the expand migration of release N+1 writes a record of each step trigger, and release N accepts the step trigger only when the record verifies against a trust root built into release N and matches the catalog. Five points are open. 1. The trust root. Options: (a) the keyless sigstore identity of the release workflow of the service, the issuer and subject that the ci-pipeline component already names as the trusted signer of the images (ST-STD-TRUST-R04), with the sigstore trusted root (Fulcio and Rekor keys) built into each release; (b) a pinned Ed25519 public key built into each release, with its private key in a key store of the CI provider; (c) both, (a) for releases and (b) for local stand-ins. 2. What is signed. Proposal: one DSSE envelope of a JSON statement with the service name, the schema history step ID, the source and target release versions and the target image digest, the table with its schema, the columns K and U, the conversion, the template version, the SHA-256 of the function source as pg_proc.prosrc holds it with its SECURITY INVOKER and search path settings, and the trigger definition as pg_get_triggerdef gives it. Release N computes the digest and the definition from the catalog and accepts the step trigger only when they are equal to the signed ones; a replayed genuine record then admits only the genuine step. 3. Verification with no network at start. The record is signed in CI at build time, because its content is a build output, and the image carries it; the expand migration writes it to a table of stego_schema. With (a), the record carries the full sigstore bundle (certificate chain, Rekor inclusion proof and signed entry timestamp), and release N verifies it with the trusted root built into it, with no call to Fulcio or Rekor. With (b), release N verifies the Ed25519 signature only. 4. Rotation. Rule for both options: release N+1 is signed only by a root or a key that release N trusts. With (a), a change of the workflow identity or of the sigstore trusted root ships first in a release that trusts both the old and the new one, and only the release after it is signed by the new one. With (b), each release carries the current key and the next key, signs with the current key, and a rotation takes two releases. A record that no trusted root verifies is refused, and the start fails closed with a fault that names the step and the remedy (deploy the intermediate release). 5. Local and unsigned builds. Options: (a) fail closed: a build with no trust root accepts no step trigger, and the local suites use a local stand-in signer whose key the local build trusts, so the expand and contract path stays testable locally (AGENTS.md: a local stand-in for each hosted system); (b) a build with no trust root accepts a step trigger by the strict (c) rules and the interim rule (d) only, and logs a warning. In both options, a release-grade build without its trust root is refused by the release gate, so a production release never runs without it. Recommendation: 1 (c), with (a) for releases, because it reuses the signer identity that the images already have and adds no secret, and (b) only for the local stand-in; 2 as proposed; 3 as proposed; 4 the accept-both rule as stated; 5 (a), because (b) would make the strongest rule depend on how a build was made. Build after the strict (c) PR of the schema builder, which this extends. Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: the recommendation, with three conditions. 1 (c): the keyless sigstore identity of the release workflow, with the sigstore trusted root built in, for releases, and a pinned Ed25519 key only for the local stand-in; a release-grade build never trusts the stand-in key: the release gate refuses a release-grade build whose built-in trust set holds a key that is not a release key, and a test proves it. 2 as proposed, and the envelope also binds the database and tenant scope it applies to (the service name and the schema), so a record cannot be replayed on the database of another service. 3 as proposed, and the table of stego_schema that holds the records is in the schema manifest. 4 as proposed, with the fault that names the step and the remedy. 5 (a), fail closed, with the local stand-in signer for the local suites (ST-STD-LOCAL); the private key of the stand-in signer is only in test fixtures, never a production key of the repository and never in a secret of CI. It is built after the strict (c) PR of the schema builder; the manifest reviewer and a second reviewer of the sigstore verification review it.

title: Must the committed record of what a service was built from hold the build identity of the stego binary that applied it?
description: Each PR that regenerates the examples writes, in examples/*/.stego/state.yaml, the build identity of the stego binary that applied it (revision, module_version and source_state of the compiler) and the registry_content_sha256. Two PRs that both regenerate always write different values on these lines, so the second one conflicts after the first merges, even when no component or generated file differs (#253, #261 and #262 on 2026-11-13). The orchestrator now resolves this at merge time with a regeneration from a clean clone (agents/followups/regenpr.sh), which costs a build and two applies per PR and one more CI run. The record is the one of ST-GEN-UC01-R05 (apply writes the record inside the service's repo). Options: (a) keep the build identity in the committed record, and keep the regeneration at merge time; (b) keep the build identity, but write it to a file beside the record that is not committed, such as .stego/build.yaml in .gitignore, so the committed record changes only when a component, a pin or a generated file changes; (c) keep it in the record, but let the examples' CI job compare the record with the build identity left out, and commit the examples with a fixed placeholder identity. Recommendation: (b), because a conflict on the committed record then means a real difference between two changes, and the build identity still exists on each machine that applied. (b) needs a change to ST-GEN-UC01-R05's contracts if they name these fields; (c) makes the committed record false on purpose.

title: Which direction does the sync trigger of a rename copy on INSERT and on UPDATE?
description: ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 rule 3 and its template version 1 (registry/runtime/manifest/sync.go, PR #270) say: on INSERT the function only sets NEW.U from NEW.K; on UPDATE it copies U into K only when U changed and K did not, and else copies K into U. ST-SUP-RC01-OC23 says: on INSERT it sets whichever of the two columns is NULL from the other; on UPDATE it copies from the column that changed into the other, and refuses the write only when both changed to values that differ after conversion. The two records do not agree, and only OC23 lets the rename release run. Under ST-SUP-RC01-OC12 the manifest of the rename release leaves out the old column K, so that the release runs on the schema of the next release after its contract step (ST-GEN-INV34); that release writes only U. With template 1, an INSERT of that release sets U := K, which is NULL: the new value is lost, and the INSERT fails on the NOT NULL of K, which the expand step keeps (ST-GEN-UC12-R02-T01). ST-GEN-UC12-R03 cannot be met. Options: (a) change rule 3 of LC02 to the direction of OC23, and replace the body of template version 1 with it (INSERT: IF NEW.U IS NULL THEN NEW.U := fwd(NEW.K); ELSIF NEW.K IS NULL THEN NEW.K := back(NEW.U); END IF; UPDATE: when only K changed, NEW.U := fwd(NEW.K); when only U changed, NEW.K := back(NEW.U); when both changed and NEW.U IS DISTINCT FROM fwd(NEW.K), RAISE with a fixed message that holds no row value; when neither changed, nothing). No release accepts version 1 yet: it is not on main and no runtime tag exists, so the body can change without a version 2. The release before a rename must then run a runtime that holds the new body, as for OC28 (ST-GEN-INV36). (b) keep LC02 and have the rename release write both K and U; then that release needs K and cannot run after the next release drops K at contract, against ST-GEN-INV34. (c) the expand step drops the NOT NULL of K and the rename release writes only U; the INSERT still loses U under template 1, so (c) does not work alone. Recommendation: (a), with a base check that refuses a rename, retype or require step when the base pins a runtime before that version, named in the fault as the release to deploy first. Decided (a) by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: rule 3 of ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 takes the direction of OC23, and the body of template version 1 changes in PR #270 before it merges, so that no runtime on main accepts the old body and version 1 has one meaning; the base check of the runtime version goes into the rename PR. Reopened by finding F3 of the schema-change research (2026-11-13): the NULL rule of (a) breaks a renamed or retyped field with a declared default, because the release of the step omits K, which takes its default before the BEFORE trigger runs, so a non-default INSERT is refused and an explicit NULL takes the default. Decided by the orchestrator under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: the trigger takes its direction from a transaction-local writer marker, SET LOCAL stego.schema_step = '<change>', which the runtime of the release of the step sets; when the marker names the change it copies U into K, else K into U; a write that sets both columns to values that differ is still refused. This replaces the NULL rule of (a); rule 3 of ST-SUP-RP15-LC02 and ST-SUP-RC01-OC23 say so, and template version 1 changes in PR #270 before it merges.

title: How does STEGO tell the author about an upsert key with no scope on a protected entity?
description: The delta security review of PR #212 (L2, low) found that an upsert key with no scope is tenant-wide: a peer in the same tenant can take a key first, and the 409 or the update branch tells that the key exists (the known limit of ST-SUP-RP10-LC25). The orchestrator asked for a generator warning for an upsert key with no scope on an entity that has a resource type. The compiler has no warning channel: a generator can only refuse (ContextValidator) or emit files, and stego generate and stego build print no advisories. Options: (a) add an advisory channel: an optional generator interface that gives advisory lines, which the compiler collects in preflight and the commands print to stderr, with the rest-api generator giving this one; this changes what the generate use case reports. (b) Refuse an upsert key with no scope on an entity with a resource type, unless the collection states that the key is tenant-wide on purpose (a new collection setting). (c) Keep the limit and state it in ST-SUP-RC20-OC13 and the rest-crud component README only. Recommendation: (a), since other review findings also ask for warnings, and a refusal breaks declarations that are correct today.

title: Which part writes the declared relationships of a row on create, update and delete: the command runtime, as for references, or the generated fill?
description: The developer walkthrough of 2026-11-13 (step 13) found that a created row's declared relationships are never written: ST-DECL-UC06-R04 and ST-SUP-RC29-OC05 say that a create, an update and a delete enqueue the declared tuples in the row's transaction, and spicedb-authz emits Write<Entity>Relationships for that, but no generated code calls it. The creator of a project with relationship owner (subject source caller) therefore cannot read, list or extend what it created. The generated CRUD code cannot call the mapper: it needs the authorization runtime's own handle, which the command handle does not expose (ST-SUP-RP06-LC10), and the command handle's Relate refuses in a command that declares no permission, such as a public create (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05); a fill also cannot decide on a row that has no relationship yet. The runtime already writes the relation of each reference when the row is written (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05). Options: (a) the runtime writes the declared relationships as it writes references: EntitySpec gets the entity's relationships (relation, subject type, and the subject from the caller, the handle's principal, or from a field); a create touches each tuple whose subject is set, an update that changes a field subject deletes the old tuple and touches the new one, and a delete deletes each tuple, all through the authorization handle in the row's transaction, joined to its revocation, with no decision beyond the command's (as for references); spicedb-authz then emits no Write<Entity>Relationships, and RP10-LC05 and RC29-OC05 state this; a runtime pin. (b) Relate in a fill may write a declared relationship on a row that the same handle created in this transaction, with no decision, also in a command with no permission; generated create, update and delete fills call it with <Entity>Tuples; a runtime pin, and a wider fill power. (c) Expose the authorization handle to generated code; this breaks ST-SUP-RP06-LC10 (no bypass). Recommendation: (a), because it gives one path for all tuples of a row, keeps the fill's powers as they are, and makes a caller subject the principal that the runtime already holds, so a client cannot choose it (ST-DECL-UC06-R04-T04). Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (a). The command runtime writes the declared relationships of a row as it writes the relations of its references, through the authorization handle in the row's transaction, joined to its revocation: a create touches each tuple whose subject is set, the caller's subject taken from the handle's principal; an update that changes a field subject deletes the old tuple and touches the new one; a delete deletes each field-sourced tuple from the row. spicedb-authz no longer emits Write<Entity>Relationships. Built on runtime v0.86.0. Delete path decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: option (1), a filtered delete, in the next PR on runtime v0.87.0: a delete of a row enqueues, in its transaction and joined to its revocation, the delete of every tuple of the row's resource and relation, for each caller-sourced relationship and each reference; the filter always names exactly one resource type, one resource ID and one relation, and the port and the adapter each refuse an empty one; a delete of one row leaves every tuple of another row intact. Leaving stale tuples (2) is refused: the lookup and list paths would still see deleted IDs, and a stale owner tuple would grant rights to an ID that a restore or an import brings back. Security review of PR #271, decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (M1) a field-sourced relationship subject is set at create and cannot change after that; an update or a patch that changes it is refused with 400 that names the field, through a bad-request error of the runtime (ErrInvalid) that OutcomeOf maps to 400, so the runtime refusal is the guard for every interface and not the generated handlers only; a command that declares no permission may not write a field-sourced relationship, and the generator refuses that declaration; a declared transfer command for a field subject is a follow-up. (M2, L3) Every declared tuple is built and checked (the subject ID and its tenant) before the row statement; any failure after the row statement breaks the handle, so Run commits nothing; a hostile subject (*, a character that a provider ID cannot hold, the ID of another tenant) gives 400. Security review of PR #272, decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (M3) a delete filter-deletes every relation that the entity's authorization definition declares on the row's resource, a list that the generator makes from the schema, so a tuple that a fill wrote is gone too; (L2) the relay refuses the filtered delete operation unless the payload has version 2.

title: Can the creator of a row read and list it right after the create, before the relay writes its tuples?
description: The developer walkthrough rerun of 2026-11-13 (main 2a8a5ff7, tasks v1) found that a GET of the tasks of a project right after two task creates listed 1 of 2. The relay writes the tuples of a create to the provider after the commit, so for a short time the creator cannot see the new row; a later list shows both. The spec allowed this gap and did not state it: each check is at least as fresh as the revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, ST-SUP-RC29-OC02, OC04), the relay raises the floor before a tuple is done (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13), and only a revocation has a status that its writer can read (ST-SUP-RP06-LC15, LC18). A consistency option alone does not close the gap, because at commit the tuple is not at the provider and no token exists yet. Options: (a) state the gap, and give the write a status that the client can read, as a revocation has; (b) a token that the relay records and that the client sends on its next list, so the list waits for that write or reads at least as fresh as it; (c) a list option for full consistency, which does not help before the relay ran; (d) the create waits for the relay, or writes the creator's tuples itself, which goes against the outbox-only rule (ST-DECL-UC06-R06, ST-SUP-RP06-LC09). Decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-13: (a) and (b). (a) Every tuple of a create already joins the transaction's revocation (ST-SUP-RP06-LC12, ST-SUP-RC29-OC05), so the write status is the revocation status: the command runtime answers Authz-Revocation: pending and Authz-Revocation-Location on each write that enqueued a tuple, and serves the status route, which honors Prefer: wait=N within the wait cap and the waiter limit (ST-SUP-RP10-LC35, ST-SUP-RP06-LC24, ST-SUP-RC29-OC16 to OC19). A create is visible to its creator once its revocation is complete. (b) The token that the client sends is the identity of its revocation, in the request header Authz-Revocation-After; the relay records the provider's token on that revocation when it lands. The list waits, within the same bounds and with no connection held, until the revocation is no longer pending, and then runs at the floor, which is at least as fresh as the recorded token (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13); it answers the state in Authz-Revocation (ST-SUP-RP11-LC21). The client never sends a provider token, so a client cannot give the provider a crafted or a stale token, and no two tokens are compared. The emitted list handlers call it in a later change of spicedb-authz and rest-api. Extended by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: a read GET /{id} honours Authz-Revocation-After the same as a list, so a single read right after the caller's write sees it (ST-SUP-RC20-OC42); and the OpenAPI document describes the request header Authz-Revocation-After, the response headers Authz-Revocation and Authz-Revocation-Location, and the status route (ST-SUP-RC20-OC43).
